“whose minds the god of this world has blinded so that they do not believe, so that the light of the gospel will not shine in their hearts.” Some of our people, however, read the latter part first.

They attribute this to God, as something he does against those he rejects because of the great persistence of their wickedness. But since to me too this manner of interpreting the statement seems sound,

I nevertheless think it is no cause for surprise if someone is called the god of this world, when many serve him because they submit to him in their thoughts, as in the expression “the ruler [?] of this world.”
For if the apostle himself says elsewhere, “Those whose god is their belly, and whose glory is their shame,” what is surprising if he calls the devil “the god of this world”?

Our Savior himself also called him “the ruler of the world.” Likewise, the Old Testament says that the gods of the nations are not gods: they have never really existed as gods at all, but have seized for themselves the reputation of being gods.

How, then, can those passages be forcibly pressed into their service? Because of the shamelessness of their wickedness, we have explained them as far as possible according to the apostle's meaning. But all the similar passages that have been left over
should likewise be treated in the same way as these, in accordance with the meaning of the Holy Scriptures.

If, then, someone reads without deceit the whole body of the teaching of the gospel and the apostles, not only will he find not a single passage that agrees completely with the opinion of the mad Manichaeans, but he will also find proofs

in abundance and clear statements that there is one authority over everything, that a blessed and upright providence governs everything, that God's patience is wonderful, and that heavenly judgment is fearful.
Nowhere is there even the bare mention of matter or of an opposing evil authority.
As for what is written in the account of creation, “The earth was formless and empty,”
the followers of Mani vainly take it to mean that the earth is self-existent, because of the words “it was.” For Scripture had already said, “In the beginning God made heaven and earth.”
Thus, what had come into being existed, although this ordering had not yet been added to it. For this very reason Mani himself, whose name is fitting for madness, flees from the entire Old Testament,

because it contains a strong and mighty denunciation, affirming that there is one authority, and nothing explicit is found in it about the devil's rebellion. From the New Testament, however, he removed and erased many things.
He left himself the few passages that have been explained, and others like them, to introduce his novel wickedness, thinking that through them he could achieve something.
Yet through the foreknowledge of the Scriptures he had already been rebuked and rejected, for our Lord himself had said beforehand, “An enemy sowed weeds among the good seed.”
And blessed Paul added, “After one warning, avoid a heretic who causes division in thought, for you know that such a person is perverted and sins, condemning himself.”

For I did not give myself to the labor of this writing in the hope that I could change these people, who are obstinately unresponsive and whose understanding has become slack and inactive. Rather, I did so in order to warn those who are sound and watchful

against the corruption and harm these people cause, so that they may flee from them even more than from those who worship idols. About them the apostle Paul himself clearly prophesied elsewhere, saying, “The Spirit expressly says
that in later times some will depart from the faith and follow deceiving spirits and teachings of demons, through [?] the lying words of people whose consciences are seared, who forbid marriage
and require abstinence from foods that God created to be used with thanksgiving.”

For those who believe and know the truth: all God's creatures are good, and there is nothing among them to be rejected; they are received with thanksgiving. For they are made holy by the word of God and by thanksgiving.
For grace, through the apostle, had already proclaimed precisely these things about these people in this way, and had already proclaimed these things about them:
grace, through the apostle, had also written beforehand both of their condemnation and of the falsehood of their words, in truth, and that their consciences are seared.
And the things they say about marriage and also about foods—in this way it exposed their disease beforehand, before their time.
But Christ himself, the Savior of all, openly promised to establish one church throughout the inhabited earth. For this reason he rightly called it catholic, and he dwells in it as in a bride,

whom alone he had previously said he would take for himself. He gave its identifying signs so that no one would be led astray by a foreign woman who deceives by assuming its name and leads those of little understanding astray. And he says, “On this

rock I will build my church, and the bars of Sheol will not overpower it.” By “the bars of Sheol” he means everything through which those who practiced perfect zeal were destined to enter by the death of confession,
which they undertook in their own persons for the fear of God. Thus he names the sword, fire, water, and all forms of [?], for they are like gates and bars of death,
through which a person enters it suddenly, all at once. Therefore, wherever there are bars close at hand because of confession and testimony, there, plainly, is
the church of Christ. But those who think it unnecessary to die for their hope are evil, permanently and completely estranged from Christ and from his church.
Moreover, a person can also find other signs concerning the true church in this earlier saying of our Lord. For he questions his disciples and says,
“Who do people say the Son of Man is?” Therefore all those who deny that he is truly the Son of Man who came in the flesh
are not Christ's church. And a little later, when Simon says to him, “You are the Christ,” he replies, “On this rock I will build my church.” On which rock? On
this faith: “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God”—and not as the madman Mani said about him: “Christ is the fifth element,” merely in the use
of the name, and not in the precise reality of the matter and the teaching alike. Thus, he says, the Good One sent, as he puts it, one after another on many occasions.
Therefore those who, in their own teaching, do not confess the only Son of God, Jesus Christ,

in accordance with the saying, “You are the Christ,” as referring to one person, in accordance with the earlier prophecy—and this proclamation had been received from that time, indeed from long before, from the beginning—among those people,
therefore, is not the church of Christ, which knows Christ as the only Son of God, who existed before the ages, who was named in the Old Testament and proclaimed before he came in the flesh.
Here end the four discourses of Titus against the Manichaeans, translated from Greek into Aramaic.
